entries.unrelatedNote: Four occurrences across four distinct candidate SHAs, none touching packages/experimental/inspector or its dependencies. Two of the four (03a7321e23 and 6decdacb89) are First-100 process-only commits (BLOCKED-QUEUE.md/decisions-approved.md/goal.md/EXEC-STATE.json edits) touching zero product code at all -- the strongest possible unrelatedness evidence, since no source change of any kind was present when the failure occurred. The other two (c60c0f3a4f, af01a06bc96) touch only tests/release/baseline-fingerprint.spec.ts and scripts/release/baseline-fingerprint.mjs (P0-01 slice work), an unrelated package with no dependency relationship to packages/experimental/inspector. Every occurrence reruns clean with zero code changes (confirmed for af01a06bc96 via a same-SHA CI rerun, run 33473101218's second attempt, success). Failure mode each time: a single real-Worker isolated-realm-session test, consistent with a timing-sensitive worker-thread integration test, matching this repo's own history of similar fixes elsewhere (e.g. 'bind fixture servers to OS-assigned ports').
entries.backfillNote: Occurrences 9-11 were backfilled on 2026-09-05, not recorded when observed. The lag is itself the finding: this count is the evidence that the test is unstable, and BLOCKED-080's criterion -- whether the flake rate is high enough that 'a failure here is distinguishable from a real regression' stops holding -- reads THIS number to decide. A register consulted to judge its own subject's severity was recording lighter than reality, and in one direction only. Absorbing a flake into a green cell and appending its occurrence are currently two separate acts, so the first happened and the second did not; mechanizing that pairing is recorded under BLOCKED-080. Backfill is verified per run rather than accepted from a list: of seven candidate runs offered, three carried this case's failure text and four did not, so only three were added.

entries.unrelatedNote: BLOCKED-023 same-SHA divergence evidence (2026-09-02): attempt 1 and attempt 2 of CI run 33578193549 ran the byte-identical candidate commit e4390a90a29e71dea1c2d32f3943b4692b5fd933 -- attempt 1 failed this test, attempt 2 passed it, with zero code changes between attempts (a same-SHA rerun). This is the definition of non-determinism: a deterministic failure cannot flip to passing on a byte-identical retry. This test spawns a real CLI subprocess (pnpm run architecture:seams against a real on-disk fixture) as its own acceptance[3] proof, consistent with subprocess-spawning tests being this repository's highest-flake-risk class (matching the already-registered Inspector real-Worker entry's own failure mode). Independently verified: the Supervisor downloaded and byte-compared both attempts' vitest-report.json artifacts (ids 9827604568 and 9828038921) directly from GitHub before registering.
